scope.summary: Purge exposed Google-key strings from reachable GitHub history and enforce exact staged, outgoing-history, canonical verification, and remote push-protection checks without a new runtime dependency.
in_scope: Sanitize all affected GitHub branch histories and verify from a fresh remote mirror.
Add a provider-pattern scanner to the existing pinned Rust xtask.
Install repository-owned pre-commit and pre-push hooks.
Add canonical authority, topology, registry, taskboard, and verify-pr integration.
Attack the implementation through independent adversarial review.
non_goals: Google Cloud credential rotation or revocation.
New Python, Go, Docker, hosted scanner, runtime, or native dependency.
A universal proof that every arbitrary secret format is absent.
Any Ferric product capability or runtime-progress claim.
dependencies: Pinned repository Rust toolchain and existing fforager-xtask dependencies.
Supported-host Git executable already governed by build/tooling-policy.toml.
GitHub secret scanning and push protection enabled for Nuntissura/ferric_forager.

acceptance_matrix.requirement: Pre-push consumes Git's update rows and scans every complete outgoing commit tree, including all ancestry for a new branch, while deletions remain legal.
evidence: The 15-test secret_scan suite passed new-branch ancestry, deletion, tree-root, ref-name, replace-ref, binary, UTF-16, staged-index, history, hook-integrity, and value-suppression counterfactuals.
A live pre-push update from the sanitized integration head to origin/main reported findings=0.

change_evidence.pre_simplification_verdict: FAIL: reachable GitHub history contained three Google API-key strings and the repository had no mandatory before-commit or before-push credential gate.
simplification_changes: Reused the existing Rust xtask and Git rather than introducing Python, Go, Docker, a hosted service, or a new package.
Deduplicated history scanning by Git blob object ID while retaining complete commit-tree coverage.
Kept diagnostics to provider pattern ID, source identity, and line without retaining or printing secret values.
change_evidence.post_simplification_verdict: PASS: the current implementation closes the direct exposed-key and local hook gaps with no new dependency, while retaining explicit limits for unknown secret formats and GitHub cache garbage collection.

DIFF_ATTACK_SURFACES: Contract and serialization boundaries: FF-BUILD-099 authority, proof-map declarations, fixture identity, stable diagnostics, and value-suppressed output.
State and resource boundaries: stage-zero index state, outgoing ancestry, ref topology, Git object closure, bounded findings, byte limits, process output, and child deadlines.
Integration boundaries: hook files, staged hook blobs, effective core.hooksPath, Git index and object database, canonical history, worktree state, and GitHub push protection.
Gate and trust boundaries: mutable client hooks, scanner bootstrap, architecture mutation execution, verify-pr aggregation, branch protection, and residual provider-prefix coverage.
INDEPENDENT_CHECKS_RUN: Three independent read-only reviewer lanes traced Git object integrity, transport-security bypasses, resource bounds, authority linkage, and final-snapshot governance.
The focused secret scanner suite executed 22 exact tests covering staged, history, worktree, pre-push, hook-integrity, ref, tree, encoding, and bounded-finding paths.
Effective core.hooksPath resolves to build/git-hooks and both exact staged hook blobs retain executable mode 100755 with matching worktree content.
A repository-wide Google-key-pattern search, exact-index scan, outgoing-snapshot scan, all-ref history scan, and fresh remote mirror scan each reported zero matched credentials.
COUNTERFACTUAL_CHECKS: A direct tree-root push containing a credential blob is rejected through recursive tree closure even when commit traversal yields no commit.
Credential-shaped local and remote ref names are rejected independently of the referenced clean object and without emitting the ref value.
A staged disabled hook, altered worktree hook, non-executable index mode, or effective worktree-level hook-path override is rejected.
The architecture fixture now creates an isolated Git repository and fails unless exact staged-index, direct-tree pre-push, and ref-name pre-push boundaries all reject the synthetic key.
BOUNDARY_PROBES: Producer-consumer boundary: committed hook constants are compared byte-for-byte with both worktree files and exact staged index blobs.
State boundary: stage-zero index entries, deleted tracked worktree files, untracked non-ignored files, and unresolved index stages have distinct fail-closed handling.
Serialization boundary: pre-push update rows validate both ref fields and both SHA-1 or SHA-256 object fields before ancestry and object-closure traversal.
Resource and integration boundary: batched cat-file reads enforce object, byte, output, and child-time limits while dense matches cap diagnostic state.
NEGATIVE_PATH_CHECKS: Git replace refs cannot conceal a tainted outgoing object because every Git child disables replacement-object substitution.
Binary, UTF-16 little-endian, UTF-16 big-endian, GitLab, Google, and credential-shaped source-label cases reject without exposing matched values.
Malformed update rows, missing objects, unsupported object types, oversized blobs, excessive input, and timed-out Git children fail closed.
Canonical history rejects credential-shaped existing ref names and scans direct non-commit ref roots rather than limiting closure to commits.

INDEPENDENT_FINDINGS.finding: Direct tree-root objects and credential-shaped ref names bypassed outgoing traversal; recursive tree closure and both ref fields now reject them.
Worktree-only hook checks could approve a disabled staged hook or ineffective configuration; exact index bytes, mode, and effective configuration now gate execution.
The initial provider corpus missed GitLab tokens and UTF-16 representations; table-driven byte scanning now rejects the named encoded cases.
Git replacement refs could substitute clean objects during outgoing inspection; every scanner Git process now disables replacement-object resolution.
Per-object processes and dense line rescans amplified resource use; batched object reads, incremental lines, and bounded finding retention now constrain the path.
Compiler failures could reproduce credential-bearing source text before scanning; hook bootstrap now suppresses compiler streams and emits one generic diagnostic.
Canonical history omitted existing ref names and non-tag custom object roots; all refs now contribute redacted names and non-commit object closure.
The first FF-BUILD-099 fixture mislabeled an in-memory matcher as snapshot integration; the replacement executes isolated production Git boundaries.

RESIDUAL_UNCERTAINTY: Client-side Git hooks and their worktree-built scanner remain locally bypassable or mutable by a hostile operator; independent GitHub push protection is the remote provider-pattern backstop, while unknown, split, compressed, or unstructured credential formats remain outside the explicit corpus ceiling.
